findings.reason: The protected source is the standard two-draw rejection sampler wrapped by a minimal deterministic adapter. Its 49-cell construction, 40-cell acceptance set, modulo mapping, retry loop, cyclic stream closure, and output trace are all concise and conventional, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode frontend problem 470, native question 903, and the Python rand10 interface. The app contract accurately separates its nonempty eventually-accepting rand7_values stream and draws count from LeetCode's no-argument method. Expected O(draws) time and O(draws) returned-trace space match the adapter; a native call has expected constant time and O(1) auxiliary space.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064968568. Its two rand7 calls, base-7 cell construction, cell <= 40 acceptance rule, and 1 + (cell - 1) % 10 mapping are identical to the protected nested rand10. The only additions are the deterministic rand7 provider and repeated app-trace collection required by the local contract.

The 64, 256, and 1024 requested outputs span 16x and isolate linear result generation with immediately accepted deterministic pairs. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.98x the reference runtime. With a transient 10,000,000-line safety allowance so a terminating manual-copy control could finish, that correct quadratic control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 142.06x.

The Approach exactly derives the 49 equiprobable cells, the unbiased 40-cell mapping, rejection probability, expected 49/40 attempts and 49/20 rand7 calls per output, deterministic stream behavior, unbounded randomized worst case, returned-list space, and entropy-recycling follow-up.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves both uniform ranges, the rand7-only and no-built-in-random restrictions, the internal n distinction, all three possible-output examples, the sole constraint, both follow-up questions in order, and the absence of visuals or tables.
